slides.0.title: Hungarian Wine Types and Styles
slides.0.subtitle: From Tokaji Aszú Sweet Wine to Egri Bikavér Bull's Blood
slides.1.title: Sweet White Wines: Tokaji Aszú and Szamorodni
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Tokaji Aszú
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Hungary's most celebrated wine — made from botrytised grape paste, with residual sugar of 120 g/L and above; layered with honey, apricot and candied orange peel
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Szamorodni
slides.1.highlights.1.content: "Szamorodni" means "as it was grown" — whole clusters are harvested (both botrytised and normal berries); the wine can be dry (Száraz) or sweet (Édes)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Eszencia
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Pure Aszú berry juice pressed by gravity alone; sugar 450–800 g/L; the world's rarest sweet wine, produced only in the finest years
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Oak Ageing
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Traditional Tokaji is aged in Hungarian oak (Zemplén) or Aszú barrels, gaining oxidative complexity — brown spices, hazelnut, beeswax, ginger
slides.1.content:
Tokaj produces three distinct sweet wine styles, each with its own production method, sweetness level and character.

🍯 Tokaji Aszú

  • Process: Aszú berries soaked in new base wine for 12–60 hours, then pressed
  • Standard: ≥120 g/L residual sugar (since 2013)
  • Ageing: Minimum 18 months oak + 12 months bottle = 30 months total
  • Flavour: Honey · apricot jam · candied orange · ginger · cinnamon · flint mineral

🎭 Szamorodni

  • Process: Whole-cluster harvest, no sorting of Aszú berries, natural fermentation
  • Dry (Száraz): Oxidative ageing like Fino Sherry — hazelnut, beeswax, almond
  • Sweet (Édes): Higher residual sugar retained — honeyed but less intense than Aszú

💎 Eszencia

  • Process: Pure Aszú berry juice pressed by gravity alone — no mechanical pressing
  • Sugar: 450–800 g/L — denser than honey
  • Alcohol: Usually only 2–5% (extreme sugar limits fermentation)
  • Rarity: Best vintages only; just a few litres per hectare
slides.2.title: Dry White Wines: Furmint and Olaszrizling
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Dry Furmint
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Hungary's foremost export wine of the 21st century — celebrated for high acidity, minerality and extraordinary ageing potential; top examples can age 20–30 years
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Olaszrizling (Balatoni)
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Olaszrizling from the basalt soils of Lake Balaton's northern shore is the most characterful representative of Hungary's everyday white wines
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Juhfark White Wine
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Grown only on the Somló volcanic hill; intensely high-acid and mineral; traditionally drunk on the wedding night — a precious rarity
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Szürkebarát (Pinot Gris)
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Szürkebarát grown on Badacsony's basalt soils is one of Hungary's most full-bodied whites, with smoky mineral complexity
slides.2.content:
Hungary's dry whites span a remarkable range of styles, from the internationally acclaimed dry Furmint to the volcanic mineral whites of Badacsony and the rare Juhfark of Somló.

🍋 Tokaj: Dry Furmint

Hungary's most internationally acclaimed dry white wine. High total acidity (8–9 g/L), rich minerality, and a structure that rivals great white Burgundy at its best.

Best pairings: oysters, steamed fish, blini with caviar

🌊 Balaton: Olaszrizling

Badacsony basalt gives a striking mineral freshness; Balatonfüred-Csopak limestone brings refined acidity and floral notes. Both are far more complex than plains-grown Olaszrizling.

Best pairings: baked fish, light chicken dishes, fresh mushrooms

🦁 Somló: Juhfark

An isolated volcanic hill where Juhfark is almost exclusively grown. Very high acid, intense mineral, typically low alcohol (11–12.5%); extremely closed when young — needs 5–10 years to open.

Best pairings: Hungarian fish soup (halászlé), braised pork
slides.3.title: Egri Bikavér: The Legend of Bull's Blood
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Defining Bull's Blood
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Egri Bikavér is the official multi-variety red wine of the Eger PDO, requiring at least 3 grapes (with Kékfrankos dominant), emphasising local terroir expression
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Superior Certification
slides.3.highlights.1.content: "Bikavér Superior" is the top tier, requiring passage through a rigorous blind tasting panel and certified by the Eger Winery Association
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Szekszárdi Bikavér
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Szekszárdi Bikavér is the other official Bull's Blood, from the more southerly Szekszárd region; known for a higher proportion of Kadarka
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Flavour Profile
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Red berries (strawberry, sour cherry), spices (clove, pepper), tobacco; medium body; ideal with Hungary's traditional braised meat dishes
slides.3.content:
Egri Bikavér is one of Hungary's most iconic wines — a multi-variety red blend bound by strict PDO rules and carrying a legendary backstory.

📋 Egri Bikavér Legal Specifications

Minimum varietiesAt least 3
Dominant varietyKékfrankos must have the highest percentage
Minimum KékfrankosAt least 30% (usually over 50%)
Other permitted varietiesKadarka / Merlot / Cab. Franc / Zweigelt / Pinot Noir
Standard minimum ageing18 months (oak + bottle combined)
Superior ageing24 months, minimum 12 months in oak

🆚 Egri vs Szekszárdi Bikavér

Egri Bikavér
  • Cooler northern climate
  • Higher acidity, more structured
  • More pronounced mineral and spice
  • Northern volcanic soils
Szekszárdi Bikavér
  • Warmer southern climate
  • Higher Kadarka percentage
  • More rose and oriental spice fragrance
  • Rounder, more generous style
slides.4.title: Other Important Wine Styles
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Villányi Franc
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Single-variety Cabernet Franc from Villány, subject to a strict official certification; one of Hungary's most internationally respected premium red wines
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Ice Wine (Jégbor)
slides.4.highlights.1.content: In Hungary's cooler northern regions (Tokaj, Eger), cold vintages can yield ice wine in a style similar to German or Canadian examples
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Rosé
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Hungarian rosé is led by Kékfrankos and Kadarka — crisp red-fruit style; a popular summer restaurant choice
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Sparkling Wine (Pezsgő)
slides.4.highlights.3.content: Hungary also has a traditional sparkling wine (Pezsgő) culture, led by Chardonnay and Pinot Noir; quality has improved significantly in recent years
slides.4.content:
Beyond Tokaji Aszú and Egri Bikavér, Hungary produces a diverse range of wine styles, each with a distinct regional identity.

WineRegionVarietyStyle
Tokaji AszúTokajFurmint + HárslevelűBotrytis sweet — honey, apricot, orange peel
Dry FurmintTokaj / SomlóFurmintHigh acid, mineral, white Burgundy style
OlaszrizlingBalatonOlaszrizlingCrisp, mineral, everyday white
Egri BikavérEgerKékfrankos + blendSpiced red — Bull's Blood legend
Villányi FrancVillányCabernet FrancRich red — internationally acclaimed quality
Szekszárdi BikavérSzekszárdKékfrankos + KadarkaFloral, spiced red

🎯 Key Takeaways

  • Sweet wine ambassador: Tokaji Aszú (botrytis · Furmint)
  • White wine ambassador: Dry Furmint (mineral · high acid)
  • Red wine legend: Egri Bikavér (Bull's Blood · multi-variety blend)
  • Top red: Villányi Franc (Cab. Franc · warm southern climate)

slides.6.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
Which famous wine style does Szamorodni Száraz (dry) most closely resemble?
A. Alsace Riesling — crisp and aromatic
B. German Auslese — nobly sweet
C. Spanish Fino Sherry — oxidative ageing with hazelnut, beeswax and almond
D. Champagne — lively and yeasty

Szamorodni Száraz undergoes oxidative ageing in partially filled barrels, developing the characteristic nutty, waxy, dried-fruit complexity found in Fino Sherry. The resulting flavour profile — hazelnut, beeswax, almond and orange peel — is strikingly similar, though Szamorodni is made from Furmint rather than Palomino and has its own distinct Tokaj character.
Which Hungarian white wine is famously very "closed" when young and needs years to reveal itself?
A. Dry Furmint from Tokaj
B. Olaszrizling from Badacsony
C. Juhfark from Somló
D. Szürkebarát from Badacsony

Somló Juhfark is one of Hungary's most unusual wines. It is almost entirely confined to this single isolated volcanic hill and is characterised by extremely high acidity, powerful mineral intensity and low alcohol (typically 11–12.5%). In its first 1–3 years the wine is tight and impenetrable; it usually requires at least 5–10 years to begin opening up and showing its full complexity.
What is the most basic legal requirement for Egri Bikavér?
A. Must come from the Eger PDO, using at least 3 grape varieties, with Kékfrankos as the dominant variety
B. Must be 100% Kékfrankos from Eger
C. Must be aged for a minimum of 3 years
D. Must pass a mandatory blind-tasting panel

The fundamental legal requirements for Egri Bikavér are: the wine must come from the Eger PDO; it must be a blend of at least 3 grape varieties; and Kékfrankos must constitute the highest single percentage in the blend. A higher-tier "Superior" certification also exists, requiring stricter standards including a blind-tasting panel and longer oak ageing.
Which Hungarian wine has its own dedicated official certified brand and is the most internationally recognised single-variety red?
A. Egri Bikavér
B. Szekszárdi Bikavér
C. Villányi Franc
D. Kékfrankos from Sopron

Villányi Franc is the only Hungarian wine with its own officially certified brand designation — a strict PDO within a PDO that governs variety, yields, alcohol level and ageing requirements. The wine critic Michael Broadbent famously called Villány the "natural home" of Cabernet Franc, and today Villányi Franc regularly achieves the highest international scores of any Hungarian red wine.
